run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The only failing user-facing path in the hotel-reservation namespace is the recommendation path: frontend's HTTP GET /recommendations returns 500 because its gRPC client span /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations is recorded as an error, while every other frontend endpoint examined (GET /hotels and its search, geo, rate, profile, reservation calls) returned 200 with successful child spans in the same seconds. The recommendation pod itself is up: the deployment reports 1/1 ready, the pod is Running with 0 restarts, its endpoint 10.244.7.237:8085 exists, and its own log shows a successful MongoDB session and a successful Consul registration at 11:34:25Z. A NetworkPolicy named deny-all-recommendation was created in namespace hotel-reservation at 2026-11-21T11:34:29Z, selects exactly the recommendation pods (io.kompose.service=recommendation) and declares policyTypes [Ingress, Egress] with no ingress and no egress rules, i.e. it isolates those pods; the first observed recommendation failures start at 11:34:38Z, after that policy existed. No recommendation server span appears in Jaeger and recommendation is absent from Jaeger's service list, which is consistent with its traffic and span export being blocked, but packet-level denial was not directly observed and change history is not integrated, so the causal step is stated as a strong hypothesis rather than a fully proven fact. A second candidate, the mongo admin-privilege revocation scripts held in ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate, was considered and rejected: geo served successful /geo.Geo/Nearby spans and logged a successful DB session during the failure window.

claims.text: NetworkPolicy hotel-reservation/deny-all-recommendation exists with podSelector matchLabels {io.kompose.service: recommendation} and policyTypes [Ingress, Egress]; its ingress and egress rule lists are empty, so it denies all ingress to and all egress from the recommendation pods.

The NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation has metadata.creationTimestamp 2026-11-21T11:34:29Z, while the recommendation Deployment's pod template label set is {io.kompose.service: recommendation}, so the policy applies to the running recommendation pod.

In a 20-trace error-filtered sample of the frontend service covering 11:34:38.157855Z-11:34:41.934535Z, every error row is on the recommendation path: 20 spans 'HTTP GET /recommendations' with error=true and http.status_code=500, and 20 spans '/recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations' (frontend client spans) with error=true and otel.status_code=ERROR, durations 26-2290 us.

The complete stored trace 6aa08486ed33b2e5 (start 11:34:40.459Z) contains only two spans, both frontend: the server span HTTP GET /recommendations (error, http.status_code=500) and its child /recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations (error, otel.status_code=ERROR); no recommendation-service server span is present in it.
Jaeger's service list for this target contains frontend, geo, profile, rate, reservation, search and user, and does not contain recommendation.

The recommendation pod is up and unchanged by restart: deployment recommendation reports ready=1, available=1, replicas=1, updated=1; pod recommendation-86cf75495d-gnzcv is Running on sregym-worker2 with restart count 0; and the Service endpoint for recommendation resolves to 10.244.7.237:8085.

The recommendation container's own log ends at 11:34:25.208742Z with a successful MongoDB session and 'Successfully registered in consul' for name srv-recommendation, id db3abc05-7d59-4e04-953f-057e1fb58748, address 10.244.7.237:8085; it records no error and no request handling after that point.

Other frontend paths were working in the same seconds: a 5-trace sample of frontend spans with http.status_code="200" (11:34:41.678Z-11:34:41.974Z) shows HTTP GET /hotels 200 (3723-5193 us) with successful children /search.Search/Nearby, /profile.Profile/GetProfiles, /reservation.Reservation/CheckAvailability, and downstream search->/geo.Geo/Nearby, search->/rate.Rate/GetRates, geo server span /geo.Geo/Nearby (38-136 us), profile, reservation and memcached spans, none with error status.

The geo service logged a successful MongoDB session and test-data generation at 11:34:26Z against mongodb-geo:27017 and then registered srv-geo; no authentication or database error line appears in its log.

Namespace hotel-reservation contains ConfigMaps named failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate holding revoke/restore scripts for the MongoDB 'admin' user's readWrite role on geo-db and rate-db respectively (revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh, revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh, revoke-mitigate-*).

Events in hotel-reservation within the window are only scheduling/rollout Normal events (ScalingReplicaSet, SuccessfulCreate, SuccessfulDelete, Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started) plus two FailedScheduling warnings on superseded mongodb-geo-78487c9767-p5545 and mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf-4kd9g pods whose message is 'pod does not exist any more'; no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff, Unhealthy or Failed reason appears for any hotel-reservation pod.

The root cause of the /recommendations 500s is the NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation: it isolates the recommendation pods from all ingress (frontend's gRPC calls) and all egress (its MongoDB, Consul and Jaeger span export), which explains why the pod is ready but frontend's client call errors, why no recommendation server span exists in Jaeger, and why the recommendation container logs nothing after its startup registration at 11:34:25Z while the policy was created at 11:34:29Z and failures begin at 11:34:38Z.

MongoDB admin-role revocation on geo-db or rate-db (the scenarios scripted in ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo/failure-admin-rate) is not the current cause: geo itself served successful /geo.Geo/Nearby spans with no error status during the failure window and logged a successful DB session, and rate also served successful /rate.Rate/GetRates spans.

A crash, OOM or eviction of the recommendation workload is not the mechanism: the pod is Running with restart count 0, the deployment is 1/1 ready and updated, the container has no previous instance, and no Evicted/OOMKilled/BackOff/Unhealthy/Failed event exists for hotel-reservation pods in the window.

Delete or amend NetworkPolicy hotel-reservation/deny-all-recommendation (for example replace it with an explicit allow rule for ingress from the frontend pods on port 8085 and egress to mongodb-recommendation:27017, consul:8500 and the tracing collector), then re-check GET /recommendations for HTTP 200 and re-check that recommendation server spans reappear in Jaeger.

gaps: Change history is not integrated (not_integrated: change_history), so I could not determine who or what created NetworkPolicy deny-all-recommendation at 2026-11-21T11:34:29Z; the creation time comes from the object's creationTimestamp read at query time.

Packet-level denial was not observed: frontend's gRPC client spans carry no error detail fields (error_details empty) and the frontend container logged only startup lines (last line 11:34:29.967Z), so the exact transport error text is unknown; why the client span fails in 26-122 us rather than timing out is not established.

Prometheus has no OTel span/RPC series for this target: get_metric_names for {__name__=~"rpc_.*|traces_.*|http_server.*|app_.*"} returned nothing over both the last hour and the full authorized window, and sum by (service_name)(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total[10m])) returned no series, so error rate and latency could not be quantified and the metric/label names rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, traces_span_metrics_calls_total, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count were not available for hotel-reservation.

Error evidence covers only a narrow slice: the error-filtered frontend trace sample is limited to 20 traces (incomplete: backend returned as many traces as requested) spanning 11:34:38.157Z-11:34:41.934Z, and a traces_search for the recommendation service over 11:00-11:34:42Z returned no data, so I cannot state how long the recommendation path has been failing or whether it recovers after 11:34:42Z.

The recommendation container writes no log lines after 11:34:25.208Z, so I could not read its side of the failure (for example refused MongoDB writes or failed span export); whether it receives any traffic at all is unknown.
HPA, resource quota and cluster-wide policy interactions were not examined; only one NetworkPolicy exists in hotel-reservation, but I did not verify that the CNI enforces policy on this cluster.

data.remove-admin-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

echo "Removing admin user..."

mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.dropUser('admin');"

echo "Admin user removed successfully"
data.revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
# TARGET_DB="rate-db"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Downgrading admin user privileges..."

# Connect to MongoDB and revoke roles
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.revokeRolesFromUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: 'readWrite', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges downgraded"
data.remove-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Recreating admin user..."

# Connect to MongoDB and create the admin user
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

echo "Admin user recreated"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges restored successfully"

data.k8s-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"

ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

TARGET_DB="geo-db"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"

echo "Waiting for MongoDB to start..."
until mongo --eval "print('waited for connection')" > /dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done
echo "MongoDB started"

# Create the admin user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating admin user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

# Create the root user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating root user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ROOT_USER', pwd: '$ROOT_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database to root
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ROOT_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ROOT_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"


echo "Initialization script completed"
